 Most recent Most popular Post published at 16:29 GMT 16:29 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 As this is Liverpool's final Premier League game before Remembrance Day, there will be a period of silence as the Last Post is played and wreaths are laid. 
 15 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Such a journey for Nyoni published at 16:28 GMT 16:28 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Aadam Patel 
Football Reporter at Anfield 
 Such a journey for Trey Nyoni. He made his Liverpool debut as a 16-year-old under Jurgen Klopp in 2024 and after the departure of Curtis Jones in the summer, Nyoni has seized his opportunity in style.
 He was arguably the standout story of Liverpool's pre-season tour and Andoni Iraola has constantly been full of praise for the 19-year-old since.
 Against Chelsea in midweek, Nyoni had more touches than anyone else on the pitch. Now it's time see how he fares in his first Premier League start against none other than the reigning champions.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 45 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:27 GMT 16:27 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 The Arsenal fans are doing their best to chant over the top of You'll Never Walk Alone. 
 I think we could be in store for a cracker here (hopefully)!
 67 17 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:26 GMT 16:26 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Liverpool proved me wrong against Brighton last week, because they didn't just win, they played well too.
 After conceding so many goals last season, you can see they have really tightened things up. Arsenal don't give much away either, so this is going to be very close.
 Alexander Isak is scoring goals again for the Reds, and they will be full of confidence coming into this game.
 You could make a case for it ending up a repeat of the result we saw at the end of last season, when Dominik Szoboszlai's brilliant free-kick meant Liverpool edged a 1-0 win.
 I do think we will see the same scoreline, just with a different winner.
 Sutton's prediction: 0-1

 Isak starting to shine published at 16:25 GMT 16:25 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Liverpool's £125m man has come to life this season. 
 Alexander Isak was not the striker we were used to seeing last campaign but he's now got six goals in seven games.
 Will he net again today?
 71 24 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Liverpool aren't underdogs' published at 16:24 GMT 16:24 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Nedum Onuoha 
Former Man City defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 When they do play Arsenal at home, why would they ever perceive themselves to be an underdog? They've won this game [at Anfield] so many times that you can't just have the idea in your head that because Arsenal are champions - yes they are the most consistent, but there are certain situations, where you will really like your chances.
 It doesn't matter who goes to Anfield. They'll really and truly be up for it. At times they have a style of play that will sort of matchup against an Arsenal side.
 70 21 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Sense of optimism around Anfield published at 16:21 GMT 16:21 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Aadam Patel 
Football Reporter at Anfield 
 There's certainly a sense of optimism around Anfield today.
 It's fair to say that Andoni Iraola has already had a positive start to life at Liverpool but a result today would deliver a real statement to the rest of the Premier League.
 "It has also felt like the connection with Anfield is growing and that is something that gives me a lot of satisfaction," Iraola writes in his programme notes.
 This is the fourth home game in a row for Liverpool and having won the previous three, Iraola will be hoping for more of the same.
 97 23 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:20 GMT 16:20 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher believes Liverpool are the biggest title challengers to Arsenal, , external though, speaking on Friday, Andoni Iraola insisted it was too early to look at the table.
 But what do you think?
 27 26 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I expect big chaos' published at 16:19 GMT 16:19 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Arsenal 
 Defender Gabriel Magalhaes, speaking to Sky Sports on if the Gunners are motivated by trying to become the first Arsenal team to win at Anfield in the Premier League since 2012: "I think so. We know it's tough to come here, they have a really good team. It's tough to play here against them. It's an opportunity to get the three points and we are ready for this.
 "We are ready for this battle today, we know it's going to be really difficult but we prepared well to come here and win"
 On what type of game he expects: "I expect big chaos in the game. We are ready, it's a big battle and we are ready."

 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Are Liverpool starting to turn a corner under Andoni Iraola? I guess we'll see after today!
 Since that 3-0 loss to Man City, the Reds have two top wins over Brentford and Brighton.

 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Just 15 minutes until kick-off. We've almost made it. 
 Are we all excited?

 Arsenal's recent form published at 16:14 GMT 16:14 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Arsenal have managed to string three wins together after that thumping at Brighton, but they've certainly been made to work. 
 Do the Gunners need to be more expressive in attack?
 55 26 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We are up for it' published at 16:13 GMT 16:13 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk, speaking to Sky Sports: "Winning obviously helps. If you look at the performances, we are getting better and improving. That's a good sign. Today is a massive game and we are really looking forward to it."
 On Arsenal: "Arsenal are a lot more than set pieces, everyone can see that. They have strength in depth but they are also very solid. We are playing against the champions so we are expecting a big game and we are up for it."
 On if it's too early to be looking at the table and the gap to the leaders: "I'm the wrong person to ask. We are focusing on today and that focus is already too big to be thinking too far ahead. Let's go for it."
 113 15 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 What does Nyoni offer that Gravenberch can't? published at 16:11 GMT 16:11 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Julien Laurens 
French football journalist on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 He is a more defensive-minded midfielder anyway. Gravenberch was never a number six, we've said that before. It worked under [Arne] Slot at a time when you still had the momentum from Jurgen Klopp, but there is clearly something missing this season and last season; it is nothing new.
 I think Nyoni brings you a bit of that, sitting more than what Gravenberch would, and certainly more naturally. With [Alexis] Mac Allister next to him, and Florian Wirtz slightly higher up the pitch, to have somebody like him - whether he's ready or not - at least the profile is the right profile. 
 For Iraola to give Trey Nyoni his first time in the Premier League for a game like this, with how important this game is, it's clearly because there was something in midfield not working before and he thinks Nyoni is a way of fixing that issue.
 111 15 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Arsenal should put Nyoni under as much pressure as possible' published at 16:09 GMT 16:09 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Nedum Onuoha 
Former Man City defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 If I was a part of that Arsenal midfield, I would be putting Nyoni under as much pressure as humanly possible.
 I'm sure he is a very good player and deserving of the opportunity, but it doesn't necessarily mean that it's going to be a comfortable game for him. It's a great test. It's a great challenge.
 I like the fact that Iraola has made that decision to put Nyoni in because you can't just wait behind people forever, hoping for an opportunity. The biggest part of the back you can have is when they put you in instead of somebody. That is a huge, huge boost.

 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 A big chance for Trey Nyoni today. 
 You'd have to think he's got a real chance in nailing down a spot in that Liverpool midfield if he puts in a performance here.

 get involved Get Involved published at 16:05 GMT 16:05 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' to have your say 
 I much prefer Myles Lewis-Skelly at the base of midfield, it frees up Rice and Arsenal seem to play better than they do with Bruno in the team. We will see but I wouldn't be surprised to see Arsenal lose.
 Neil, Cam 
 136 187 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Szoboszlai was desperate to start' published at 16:03 GMT 16:03 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, speaking to Sky Sports on what we will learn from his team today: "A big game. We have a schedule where is not time for a lot, each two or three days you prepare a game quickly and today is a big one definitely. We have to be at our very best but we are coming from three wins from home. We needed these wins and we want to finish with a big win."
 On Trey Nyoni's first Premier League start: "The thinking is that he is playing very well, we trust him. He has good control on the ball, he understands the game well, without the ball he is smart to deal with all the complications. He is really good on those things. We have to consider we have very good subs for the second half. It gives us good options, but we definitely trust Trey to do well."
 On Dominik Szoboszlai's return to the bench: "He was desperate to start. After the Brentford game we probably went too early. We have been a bit more cautious and he will have to go through the process today he probably plays in the second half."
 On what he wants from Anfield: "What they give us every time. We can use this advantage in a proper way."
